title: Bank reconciliation & credit losses — Summit Office Supply
instructions: Summit Office Supply's controller needs the December 31 bank reconciliation and the year-end credit loss adjustment. Use the exhibits.

exhibits.title: Bank reconciliation data
exhibits.content:
- Balance per bank statement: **$84,600**
- Balance per general ledger: **$77,160**
- Deposits in transit: **$9,200**
- Outstanding checks: **$12,750**
- The bank charged Summit's account **$300** for a check written by another company (bank error).
- The bank collected a note receivable for Summit: **$5,000** principal plus **$75** interest (not yet recorded by Summit).
- Bank service charges: **$45**.
- A customer's check for **$1,200** was returned NSF.
- Check #2291 to a supplier (on account) was written and cleared for **$2,480** but recorded by Summit as **$2,840**.

exhibits.title: Receivables aging, December 31
exhibits.content:
| Age | Balance | Expected loss rate |
|---|---:|---:|
| Current | 420,000 | 1% |
| 31–60 days | 95,000 | 5% |
| 61–90 days | 40,000 | 20% |
| Over 90 days | 15,000 | 60% |

Allowance for credit losses: January 1 balance **$16,000** credit; write-offs during the year **$13,500**; recoveries **$700**. The loss rates reflect current conditions and supportable forecasts.

rows.label: Book-side adjustment for check #2291 (enter + or −)
rows.explanation: The check was 2,480 but recorded as 2,840 — cash was reduced 360 too much. **+360**.

parts.prompt: Record the single compound adjusting entry for all book-side reconciling items.
parts.explanation: Net cash change = +5,075 − 45 − 1,200 + 360 = **+4,190**. Debits: Cash 4,190; Service charge expense 45; Accounts receivable 1,200 (NSF reinstated). Credits: Notes receivable 5,000; Interest revenue 75; Accounts payable 360 (the overstated payment reduced AP by too much, so AP is restored). Total debits = credits = 5,435.

rows.label: Credit loss expense for the year
Net accounts receivable reported
rows.explanation: 570,000 − 25,950 = **544,050**. (The NSF check reinstated in the bank reconciliation is assumed to be already reflected in the aging.)
